extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, astronomers, and experimental scientists (members/readers of the Royal Society, 17th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for making, measuring, interpreting, and reporting observational and experimental natural-philosophy work (astronomical observations, meteorological/chemical observations, physiological experiments, materials descriptions) as practiced/presented to the Royal Society in the 17th century.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine satellite orbital period by comparing successive observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare multiple observations across dates to infer the number of revolutions and thus the period (e.g., compare first with third observation to find whole revolutions in 18 days, compare other pairs to exclude shorter candidate periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the relative positions at successive dates to count revolutions (look for 'almost whole ones'), combine different observation-pairs to exclude ambiguous shorter periods, and refine ephemeris as more observations accumulate; note that greater numbers of observations are required for more precise determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer interior vs exterior satellite from relative motion and position
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether a newly-seen body is an interior satellite by its motion relative to the planet and other satellite(s) (e.g., appearing between Saturn and its ordinary satellite, approaching Saturn on the west and being in the superior/inferior part of its circle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track whether the new body moves toward or away from the primary and note east/west positions relative to known satellites; sustained relative motion patterns (e.g., approaching Saturn on the west, returning in a particular part of its circle) confirm interior/exterior nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate orbital semidiameter by proportion to visible ring semidiameter
rubrics_metrics.description: Express the semidiameter of a satellite's circle relative to Saturn's ring (e.g., 'the semidiameter of this circle is three semidiameters and a fourth of Saturn's ring').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportions against an identifiable feature (Saturn's ring) visible in the instrument as a practical scale when angular measures or precise instruments are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure angular separation by timing transit differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the time difference between the passage of a satellite and the passage of the centre of the planet, and convert that time (seconds of an hour) into an angular/distance measure (e.g., 30 seconds of an hour corresponds to ~10 Saturn diameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer timing passage differences with a telescope rather than pure eye-estimates for quantitative separation estimates; record both the timing method and conversion used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer instrumented/timed measures over eye estimates when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial distance estimates may be made by eye comparing satellites with the planet, but later and better measures were made by timing passages and by using larger telescopes (examples: Campani's 17-foot, Lebas's 20-foot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish between rough visual estimates and instrument/timing-derived measures; indicate the instrument used and observers present when reporting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct and revise ephemeris after sufficient observations
rubrics_metrics.description: After several confirming observations, produce an ephemeris of the satellite's positions to be used until more precise determinations are possible; revise as later observations warrant (e.g., follow a chosen period in the ephemeris until more precise determination is obtained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State assumptions used in the ephemeris (candidate period), explain why that choice was made, and note the need for further observations for refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe meteors/snow directly in situ rather than from speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pursue fanciful or armchair theorizing; observe snow 'abroad' with the eyes well fixed and with caution during thin, calm, still snowfall to see its forms and behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field observation conditions are essential — specify meteorological context (thin, calm, still), fixate gaze to resolve regular figures, and document the sequence from largest regular forms to smaller fragments and altered flakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and document crystalline morphology of snow
rubrics_metrics.description: Report that many parts of snow are regularly figured, often as little rosettes or stars of six points, with collateral points set at the same angles as the main points; note also rarer forms (circular, hexagonal, 12-point, cylindrical shoots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the typical form as well as rarities, and illustrate or precisely describe angles, symmetry, and collateral structures to support morphological claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer formation process from observed morphology and dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: From observed shapes and interactions, infer that cloud droplets freeze in descent into icicles that shoot out points, and that later thawing, clumping, or collision produces broken or clumped flakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link observational sequence (descent, freezing by cold winds, thawing by warmer air, collisions) to resulting morphologies; report plausible causal chain rather than untested speculation and note observational evidence supporting each step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use analogical comparison to known crystalline salts and objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare snow crystals' configurations with those of nitre, lixivial salts, sal ammoniac, icicles of urine, and feathers to find resemblances that inform hypotheses about composition and formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the specific resemblances (angles, branching patterns, paired collateral shoots) and use them cautiously as analogical evidence for composition or formation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design experiments to show direct operation and consequences of variable removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate phenomena by both (a) showing direct operation of the factor (e.g., enclosed air pressure acting on bodies under water) and (b) demonstrating the changes that follow when the factor is removed or weakened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ two kinds of trials to reveal causation: direct manifestation trials and removal/alteration trials; report both types to strengthen causal claims and address objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address plausible objections with weighty considerations and experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: When a hypothesis invites plausible objections (e.g., that atmospheric pressure sufficient to have mechanical effects would crush exposed bodies), employ substantial arguments and experiments to remove the force of that objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state likely counter-arguments and provide experimental or theoretical responses demonstrating why the objection does not invalidate the primary interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and completeness in manuscript submission/registry
rubrics_metrics.description: When committing manuscripts to institutional judgment (e.g., Royal Society registry), include main parts and annexes; do not omit pamphlets or parts which would misrepresent the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/authors should ensure full copies are presented and recorded; the registry should accurately record the purposes of the MS to avoid false claims of omission or improper handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report experimental conditions and stimuli precisely (physiological experiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record environmental conditions (e.g., hearts laid on a glazed earthen white plate in a cold window), timings of observed phenomena (systole/diastole durations, total time of beating), interventions (needle prick, heating on hearth), and effects (resumption of beating after warming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise temporal and conditional detail so others can interpret, repeat, and assess the experiment; note limits of inferences (e.g., when to call an organism dead if motion persists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe disease courses and regional differences carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Report symptoms (small hard red pustule), timeline of progression (growth ~6 months, decline ~6 months), recurrence, scarring, lack of effective remedies, and regional epidemiological observations and causal hypotheses (diet, imported slaves, winds arising from marshes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give careful clinical description, duration, and outcomes; record local practices and attempted remedies; distinguish observation from conjectured causes and note competing hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate building materials by functional properties and suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess stones by quarry origin and properties: initial softness then hardening in air, grit fineness, durability in air and water, suitability for carving (Portland stone) versus resistance to fire or brittleness (Derbyshire freestone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report particular properties relevant to intended use (carving, exposure to water/fire), compare samples from different sources, and raise queries about artificial production methods where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report agricultural/technical practices with procedural steps and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing practical methods (e.g., training vines to grow over a roof), state the steps (single stem to eaves, cut off luxuriant branches, allow spreading on tiles) and the observed benefits (more sun yielding riper, sweeter grapes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear procedural directions and observed advantages or caveats so readers can reproduce and judge efficacy.
